thinking_text:
**Considering diameter adjustments**

If the outer diameter changes by 1 mm, it may help preserve the radial ligament when the hole diameter also changes by 1 mm. The capsule width might need a 1 mm change too. If I aim for increased stiffness and add more holes, I might have to adjust the outer shape to be larger, but I’m not sure in which direction. I should note that faces can serve as visual labels and might involve Brep IDs. Also, face codes look sufficient for the request.

response_json.request: Change the shape of the profile of link arms to the shape of long hole to increase its stifness. Then change the diameter of the holes by 1mm and adjust the shape accordingly.

actions.operation: Change the link-arm profile to a long-hole-shaped profile.
actions.target: the profile of the link arms
actions.relational_constraint: The modified profile must belong to and replace the existing profile of the link arms.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the link arms and their existing profile geometry in the CAD model; the dimensions and orientation of the requested long-hole shape are not specified. The model and multiview images identify the link arms as the four three-eye scissor links S03, S04, S05, and S06. Interpret the requested long-hole shape as a closed obround or stadium-shaped outer link profile, with two semicircular ends joined by tangent straight sides and aligned to the line between the two end-pivot centers. The final capsule width and end radius remain unspecified and must be selected or parameterized to increase stiffness while preserving mechanism clearance.
steps: Modify the four scissor-link sections only: front descending link S03, front ascending link S04, rear descending link S05, and rear ascending link S06. Do not modify the upper and lower rails S01 and S02 or the pins S07 and S08 during this profile operation.

Use the large planar face of each link as the sketch support: S03 face 0022 or 0034 (FACE 12 or FACE 24), S04 face 0035 or 0047 (FACE 142 or FACE 154), S05 face 0048 or 0060 (FACE 171 or FACE 183), and S06 face 0061 or 0073 (FACE 200 or FACE 212). Alternatively, edit the original master sketch from which each link was extruded.

Project or convert the three existing pivot-bore axes into the sketch. Fully constrain the two end-pivot centers and center-pivot center so their positions remain unchanged; preserving these axes is required to maintain coaxial relationships with corner pins S07 and center pins S08.
Create a construction centerline between the two end-pivot centers. Use this centerline as the longitudinal axis of the new long-hole-shaped outer profile.

Construct the new outer profile as an obround or stadium: place equal-radius semicircular end arcs concentrically on the two end-pivot centers and connect them with two parallel tangent lines. The profile must be symmetric about the end-center construction line.

Choose or parameterize the obround radius so the new link width is at least sufficient to contain the center pivot hole and its required radial ligament. Because the stated intention is increased stiffness, avoid reducing the minimum transverse width or the net section around any pivot hole.

Where the center eye must remain locally larger than the selected capsule width, retain a symmetric tangent enlargement around the center pivot rather than creating an abrupt notch. Join it to the capsule sides with tangent arcs or spline segments having curvature continuity.

Trim and remove the former segmented strap-and-three-lobe outer profile represented by the end-eye walls, center-eye arcs, and straight edge walls. Preserve all three pivot-hole centers and preserve the existing link thickness.

Extrude the revised closed profile to the original thickness, or update the existing pad/extrusion feature so the link remains in its original Z layer. Maintain the front/rear offsets and the alternating link layers visible in the left, right, top, bottom, and isometric views to prevent interference at the crossings.

Reapply the existing small edge fillets to the new perimeter. Use equal fillet radii on corresponding front and rear links, and do not allow the fillets to break into the pivot bores or reduce the required bearing length.
Mirror or copy the same parameterized profile logic between corresponding links S03/S05 and S04/S06 while retaining their opposite diagonal orientations and existing assembly positions.

Regenerate the assembly and check the full scissor travel. Confirm that the revised outer profiles do not collide with each other at the center crossing, with rails S01 and S02, or with the walls of the elongated rail slots.

actions.operation: Change the diameter of the holes.
actions.relational_constraint: Perform this modification after changing the link-arm profile.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify which holes are intended and determine whether the 1 mm diameter change is an increase or a decrease, since the direction is not specified. Based on the referenced link arms and the instruction sequence, the most likely targets are all three pivot bores in each of S03, S04, S05, and S06, for a total of twelve link holes. The rail slots and rail fixed-pivot bores are not included unless explicitly requested. The diameter direction must remain a signed parameter, with D_new = D_existing plus or minus 1 mm, until clarified.
steps: Locate the twelve cylindrical link bores: S03 faces 0025, 0028, and 0032 (FACE 27, FACE 25, and FACE 26); S04 faces 0038, 0041, and 0045 (FACE 157, FACE 155, and FACE 156); S05 faces 0051, 0054, and 0058 (FACE 186, FACE 184, and FACE 185); and S06 faces 0064, 0067, and 0071 (FACE 215, FACE 213, and FACE 214).
Edit the diameter constraint of the circular cuts in the link master sketch or edit the corresponding hole/cut features. Do not move any hole center.

Define a signed change parameter delta_D with an absolute value of 1 mm. Set each revised diameter using D_new = D_existing + delta_D. Obtain confirmation whether delta_D is positive or negative before committing the final dimensions.
Apply the same signed diameter change to the two end holes and center hole of every link unless a hole-specific exception is provided. Keep corresponding front and rear links geometrically matched.
Cut each revised circle through the full link thickness using a through-all or up-to-last cut so the cylindrical bore remains continuous through the part.

Preserve coaxial alignment between the end bores and the four corner pin shafts S07, and between the center bores and the two center pin shafts S08. The corner-pin shaft faces used for verification are 0075, 0078, 0081, and 0084; the center-pin shaft faces are 0087 and 0090.
Do not change the lower rail fixed bore 0006, upper rail fixed bore 0017, lower rail slot faces 0007 through 0010, or upper rail slot faces 0018 through 0021 as part of this action.

After regeneration, verify pin-to-bore fit. If the hole diameter is increased, confirm that the resulting clearance does not exceed the allowable joint play. If the hole diameter is decreased, confirm that the existing S07 and S08 pins still fit with the required running or bearing clearance.
Check the remaining radial material from each revised bore to the new obround perimeter and confirm that no hole cut intersects an outer fillet or creates an inadequate net section.

actions.operation: Adjust the shape to correspond to the changed hole diameter.
actions.relational_constraint: The adjustment must be consistent with the preceding 1 mm change to the hole diameter.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify which shape is to be adjusted, how it relates to the modified holes, and what geometric adjustment is required. The functional interpretation is to adjust the new obround outer profile and the local material surrounding each pivot hole so that the original radial ligament or edge distance is maintained after the signed 1 mm hole-diameter change. If constant radial ligament is required, the corresponding local outer diameter or capsule width changes by the same signed 1 mm diametral amount. This rule must be reconciled with the stiffness objective and assembly-clearance limits.
steps: Return to the parameterized obround-profile sketches for S03 through S06 after applying the signed 1 mm bore-diameter change.

Measure or retrieve the original minimum radial ligament between each pivot bore and its surrounding outer profile. Define this as a controlled parameter rather than leaving the outer profile unconstrained.

Constrain the end-arc radius by R_outer_end = D_hole_end divided by 2 plus the required radial ligament. If the radial ligament is to remain unchanged, a 1 mm diametral hole change produces a corresponding 0.5 mm radial change and a 1 mm change in the associated local outer diameter.
Constrain any retained center-eye enlargement by R_outer_center = D_hole_center divided by 2 plus the required center-eye ligament. Keep the center enlargement concentric with the center bore.

For a uniform capsule profile, set the capsule half-width to the largest required outer radius among the end and center regions. This avoids a weak narrowed section and best supports the stated stiffness intention.

If packaging prevents a fully uniform capsule width, blend the center-eye region into the parallel obround sides with tangent arcs. Avoid sharp re-entrant corners and maintain equal geometry on opposite sides of each link centerline.

Where the hole diameter is increased, enlarge the associated outer profile as required to preserve ligament and stiffness. Where the hole diameter is decreased, do not automatically reduce the outer profile if doing so would conflict with the stated stiffness increase; retain the larger profile unless assembly clearance requires otherwise.
Recalculate and reapply perimeter fillets or chamfers after the profile update. Keep fillet sizes subordinate to the minimum ligament so they do not weaken the pivot-eye regions.
Propagate the adjusted dimensions to all four links using shared parameters or linked sketches. Preserve S03/S05 correspondence and S04/S06 correspondence, including their front/rear offsets.
Regenerate the complete mechanism and perform interference checks at both center pivots, all four corner pins, the upper and lower rails, and both elongated guide slots.

Verify the mechanism at its most collapsed and most extended positions. Confirm that the wider or adjusted obround profiles do not contact adjacent links and that the slotted corner pins retain their full intended travel.

Perform a final stiffness-oriented design check using minimum net section, section width, stress concentration around the three bores, and out-of-plane clearance. Retain the original link thickness unless a separate thickness change is explicitly authorized.

intention: Increase the stiffness of the link arms.
